slots.title: A phone propped up at home showing the treatment hub: mat, mug, late light
slots.brief:
Brand: Pelvy, "Pelvic health, between appointments.".
Category: Digital health, Pelvic health, Clinician tools.
Positioning: For pelvic health clinicians whose patients lose the thread between appointments, Pelvy is the between-appointments companion that puts the clinician's own advice, exercises and reminders on the patient's phone, because it was built by a practising pelvic health physiotherapist from what patients and clinicians asked for. Unlike a handout or a Kegel timer, it counts the patient through the whole program and keeps the advice where they will find it. Said plainly: what you tell your patients in the room, still with them at home.
Visual school: Warm humanist.
Signature element: The clinician's note: the words a clinician gave their patient, set in Literata on a sage card and signed with the clinician's name. It is the app's notes feature promoted to the brand's lead image, because it is the whole promise in one object: what your clinician told you, still with you at home.
Palette: #41684A, #5E6687, #78A080 (the first is the brand colour). Proportion: Mostly paper and white. Deep sage carries the mark, headings that need colour, and solid buttons. Sage, the 2024 colour, is for large quiet fills behind dark text and for the illustration grounds, and never sits under white text. Slate appears once per view at most, on the one action that matters. Ink carries the reading.
Art direction: The app is the picture. The lead image on any Pelvy surface is a real screen from the app: the clinician's note, the count, a program. Photography is the setting around it: the corner of a home where the exercises get done, and the treatment room. Rooms, objects and hands before faces. Movement is shown with stills from the app's own exercise videos, never drawn.
Treatment: Natural light, warm when it is warm: late afternoon through a curtain, morning through a clinic window. True colour, never tinted green. Sage turns up on its own in a mat, a wall or a plant. Lived-in and slightly untidy beats styled. Photographs take the 22 pixel radius and leave a quiet third for type.
Always: Lead with a real app screen, flat and legible, at phone proportion with the panel radius.; Photograph the real clinic and the real home setting, including the slightly worn bits.; Use stills from the app's own exercise videos for anything that demonstrates a movement.; Credit clinicians by name and role, with a signed release on file.; Show every kind of body Pelvy is for across a set: different ages, sexes and sizes.; Leave a quiet third of the frame for type..
Never: No drawn phones and no rendered 3D devices. Show the screen itself, or a real phone in a real photograph.; No illustrated people of any kind.; No fruit, flowers or shells standing in for anatomy.; No women-only casts. Pelvy is for everyone with a pelvis.; No generated images of people, ever. Generated photography is limited to rooms and objects, and is labelled.; No posed wellness: no white linen, no hands on a bare belly, no sunrise yoga.; No screen that shows a real patient's name or note..
The shot: A phone propped up at home showing the treatment hub: mat, mug, late light. Why it exists: The website hero and the poster need the app in the place it is used.
Format: 16:9, for web.
No text, lettering, logos, signage or watermarks anywhere in frame. The real mark is added afterwards from the vector master, never drawn by the model.
Nobody in frame may be presented as a real customer or member of staff: this is a sample of the direction, and it is labelled as generated wherever it appears.
